column1: # Ratchet baseline for Test.Parity: corpus <TAB> check <TAB> total <TAB> passing.
# `passing` is how many checks of that kind passed when this file was written.
# The test fails when the current number is LOWER, so the later waves lower
# these numbers instead of touching the corpora. `total` must always equal the
# real number of checks, which pins the corpus files against silent truncation.
# Check kinds:
#   w2u / u2w      - the converted text against the reference
#   roundtrip      - our W->U->W->U must land where the reference lands
#   w2u-warnings   - our warning TEXTS against the exported reference texts
#   u2w-warnings   - whether we warn at all on the way back (the corpus records
#                     only a count there, and the back-conversion texts are
#                     not exported yet)
# Wave 2 brought w2u from 24 to 28 (jsewts) and 25 to 29 (Lingua): the
# bracketed foreign text, the escapes and the dropped line breaks now match.
# Almost every remaining warning gap is a syllable-level one ("Subjoined y not
# expected after r", "Invalid prefix consonant", "more than one ^"), i.e. the
# orthography rules of wave 3, plus "No Tibetan characters found!" from wave 4.
# Wave 3.3 (the generic stack renderer) brought w2u from 28 to 185 (jsewts),
# 29 to 188 (Lingua), 0 to 14 (ewts-rs) and 1 to 4 (java): syllables the book
# did not spell now render with the references' marks - subjoined letters,
# vowels, carets - so the word-shape checks of w2u mostly pass. The u2w leg
# is untouched by that wave (it does not run the generic stack). The roundtrip
# gains (37->175 / 38->177) are the same shapes proving stable through
# W->U->W->U. Remaining w2u gaps are reference quirks (repeated tshegs,
# vowel-only escapes, "blaxbla" splitting) and the warning texts.
# Wave 3.4 (per-spelling grammar arms): w2u now parses under the Wylie arms
# instead of the Tibetan arms + generic stack. Every reference corpus holds
# its numbers unchanged, and ewts-rs gains one check (14->15). The kangyur
# round-trip loses 12 lines (251->239): the u2w leg still emits "blind"
# Wylie - no dots (g.yul -> "gyul"), no implicit @a@ (མུན་གནག -> "mun gng"),
# no "sa'i" (སའི -> "s'i") - and the strict Wylie arms read those differently
# (gyul -> གྱུལ, gng -> གང, pStack s'i -> སྰི) than the permissive old path
# did.
# Wave 3.5 (mark-aware Wylie renderer, kangyur corpus): the u2w leg now
# writes dots before subjoinable stacks (གཡུལ -> "g.yul"), an implicit @a@
# before a following full letter (སའི -> "sa'i", མུན་གནག -> "mun gnag")
# and drops a leading a-chen that only carries a vowel (ཨུ -> "u"). The
# kangyur round-trip climbs back to 254, and the u2w legs gain the same
# shapes: jsewts 16->50, Lingua 15->47, java 0->1. No implicit vowel is
# written after a syllable's closing letter (ས -> "s", མངའ -> "mnga'"):
# per the spelling rules a closing mark never takes an explicit vowel, and
# writing one leaks a fresh a-chen through the back leg (ཁྱེའུས ->
# "khྱe'usa" -> ཁྱེའུསཨ).
# Wave 3.4.2 (the prefix position): the checker's first rule lands. Words that
# open with a consonant in the reference's PREFIX state now earn "Invalid
# prefix consonant" (tgra, c, pgru) or "Prefix ... does not occur before ..."
# (grla, bdza) exactly like the reference: jsewts w2u-warnings 172->177,
# Lingua 174->179. The three still-red rows (g....yag, grglam, grywa) now
# report only their prefix part; the rest of the texts wait for 3.4.3/3.4.4.
